subject: Request: Custom SLA amendment + order form language for Synapse Health
messages:
From: Emily Tran <emily.tran@synapsehealth.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurement@synapsehealth.com
Date: 2027-04-02T15:22:00-07:00
Subject: Custom SLA amendment for Synapse - MSA & order form attached

Hi Kimberly,

Thanks again for the demo last week — team was impressed with the latency profiles. Procurement and legal asked me to follow up with a formal request: Synapse needs a narrow SLA addendum attached to the MSA and reflected in the order form for our production workload. Key asks are below so your legal and sales teams can redline: 

- Availability: request 99.99% monthly uptime for primary region (we understand regional failover exceptions).
- Latency: 95th percentile inference latency target of <= 120ms for the default model at 1k qps sustained; if that requires a latency SLO exception, we want a documented mitigation plan and credits tied to percent deviation.
- Maintenance windows: allow a single recurring 3-hour monthly maintenance window outside business hours; any additional scheduled downtime must be notified 10 business days in advance.
- Credits: pro-rated service credits calculated on monthly bill for downtime beyond SLA per the order form; please provide proposed formula.
- Audit logs: 12 months retention for request/response logs for our compliance team.

Attached are the current MSA with track changes and our preferred order form template (OrderForm_Synapse_PROD.xlsx). Can you provide a redline and proposed addendum language by EOD Friday? Procurement is aiming to review and sign within two weeks pending legal approval.

Thanks,
Emily
Emily Tran
Senior Procurement Manager
Synapse Health Systems
procurement@synapsehealth.com
(415) 555-0123

Attachments: Synapse_MSA_TrackChanges.docx, OrderForm_Synapse_PROD.xlsx
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
To: Emily Tran <emily.tran@synapsehealth.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-04-02T16:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Custom SLA amendment for Synapse - MSA & order form attached

Hi Emily — thanks for the clear summary and the files. We're happy to work through this. High-level notes before legal does a formal redline:

- Availability: 99.99% is a stretch for multi-tenant hosted plans at the token volumes you described; we can offer 99.99% on Dedicated or a Dedicated-backed order form. For hosted, we typically offer 99.95% with documented fallbacks.
- Latency: we can commit to a latency SLO for a pinned model/profile on Dedicated (and provide traces); for hosted plans we can provide a 95th percentile target but would need an exception carve-out for burst events and unseen prompt distributions.
- Credits: we'll propose the standard pro-rated monthly credit table but we can add an escalator for critical regulated workloads.

Looping Marcus (SE) for technical detail on the latency SLA and Lauren for legal redlines. Marcus — can you draft an operational clause for latency SLO, mitigation steps, and monitoring signals we can include in an addendum? Lauren — can your team take a look at Synapse_MSA_TrackChanges and suggest precise order-form language for availability and credits?

Emily — we'll aim to return a consolidated redline by Friday EOD. If procurement needs faster turnaround, let me know and we'll escalate.

Best,
Kimberly Park
Head of Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference
kimberly_park@redwood.ai

From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-04-02T18:30:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Custom SLA amendment for Synapse - technical proposal

Kim — draft language below for the latency section (internal). Feel free to edit before we send externally.

--- Draft Latency SLO Clause (for addendum) ---
Redwood will maintain, for the Services identified in the Order Form, a 95th percentile request latency not to exceed 120 milliseconds measured at the Redwood edge for requests to the pinned model under steady-state production load as defined in the Order Form. Exclusions: latency measurements will exclude (a) degraded performance due to Network or Customer-side issues; (b) scheduled maintenance windows; (c) usage beyond the agreed sustained QPS outlined in the Order Form; and (d) force majeure events.

If Redwood fails to meet the latency SLO for two consecutive billing periods, Redwood will: (i) provide a written remediation plan within 5 business days; (ii) offer 25% service credit on the affected resource for the subsequent month for the first failure, escalating per failure thereafter up to a capped limit.

Tradeoffs: to achieve this SLO consistently we recommend a Dedicated deployment with reserved capacity and an autoscale buffer of 20% above projected qps. Achieving 120ms on hosted with no capacity reservation adds risk.

--- end draft ---

I also attached a short sample addendum (MSA_SLA_Redline_Sample.docx) with order-form fields called out: pinned model id, reserved qps, measurement endpoint, and credit calc.

Marcus
Senior Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference
marcus_lin@redwood.ai

Attachment: MSA_SLA_Redline_Sample.docx
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
To: Emily Tran <emily.tran@synapsehealth.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-04-03T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Custom SLA amendment for Synapse - consolidated redline coming

Emily — forwarding Marcus's proposed language and a short addendum sample for your review. Quick notes and asks: 

- We'll propose two pathways in the addendum: (A) Dedicated: 99.99% availability + 95th pct latency <= 120ms with reserved capacity and the credit table Marcus suggested; (B) Hosted: 99.95% availability + best-effort latency SLO with an explicit exception clause for bursts and prompt distribution changes.
- For audit logs, we can commit to 12 months retention for request/response metadata and delivery of a monthly log export. Full payload retention requires a privacy review; we recommend pseudonymization for compliance.
- Maintenance: we'll accept the 3-hour monthly window; we ask that Synapse allow one additional 2-hour emergency buffer per quarter for critical fixes with 48 hours notice where possible.

Lauren — please add any carve-outs or standard legal phrasing; target to produce a redline of their MSA + an order form template by EOD today.

Emily — once we have legal redline we'll circulate for your sign-off and prepare DocuSign routing. Proposed next steps: legal redline -> Synapse review (2 business days) -> finalize order form -> DocuSign. Is your internal sign-off timeline still two weeks?

Thanks,
Kimberly

Kim / team — thanks for the fast turnaround and the two-path approach — that works for our internal committees. A few quick points: 

- Dedicated preferred: Synapse will accept the Dedicated pathway. We can move forward on a Dedicated-backed order form that includes pinned model, reserved qps (1,200 sustained), and the 120ms 95th-pct latency SLO.
- Credits: acceptable as drafted; procurement would like the credit calc added to the order form spreadsheet so it can be automated in our billing system.
- Audit logs: please include the monthly export process and a sample CSV schema in the next redline.
- Timeline: procurement and legal aim to complete review by 2027-04-15. Please route final redline via DocuSign when ready to speed signature.

We received the sample addendum and will share any minor comments. Please send the order form with the credit calc and DocuSign envelope when available.
